notation.edge: A cycle-table edge is a rising SYSCLK boundary. Signal changes shown after an edge apply during the following bus cycle.
notation.asserted: Logical assertion; physical low for active-low pins in bus_signals.json.
notation.negated: Logical negation; do not equate with a driven high level on shared three-state signals.
notation.qualified_BG: BG asserted while ABB is negated and the ARTRY result after the preceding AACK is negated.
notation.qualified_DBG: DBG asserted while DBB and DRTRY are negated and the ARTRY result associated with that data tenure is negated.
notation.figure_reading: Cycle tables were transcribed from rendered figures. They state selected relative-event sampling relationships, not exhaustive per-pin/per-edge waveforms, BFM expectations, or electrical setup/hold limits. Symbolic rows such as TA, wait, and later are intentional.

assertions: An early or qualified ARTRY retries both address and data portions.

In normal DRTRY mode, the generic/64-bit late-cancel boundary is the cycle after the first/only TA. In 32-bit mode this is after the first TA for word or smaller operations, but after the second TA for double-word or burst operations.
The retried operation is not guaranteed to be the next operation reissued because the core may reorder internally.

rules: Cached 32-byte burst has eight DH[0:31] beats numbered 0 through 7 in the figure.

DL[0:31] and DP[4:7] are not sampled on reads and are driven low on writes.
The same arbitration and termination protocol as 64-bit mode applies.
Late ARTRY cancellation point for a burst is after the second TA in normal mode, or coincident with the second TA in no-DRTRY mode.
unresolved: Critical-word-first start/wrap ordering for all A[27:29] values is not yet encoded as eight explicit cycle rows.

rules: An aligned 8-byte uncached/write-through transaction uses two DH beats.
TBST remains negated even though there are two beats.
TA acknowledges each beat and each read beat can enter a DRTRY late-cancel window.
Late ARTRY for the double-word operation is permitted through the cycle after the second TA in normal mode.
unresolved: Figure 8-22 has not yet been converted into per-edge rows for its two separate DRTRY extensions.

preconditions: A read address tenure completed without ARTRY.
A later write address tenure completed without ARTRY.
Both data tenures are queued.

at_edge: In the cycle after read AACK, qualified ARTRY is sampled negated.
after_edge: Read data tenure is oldest in the queue.

at_edge: In the cycle after write AACK, qualified ARTRY is sampled negated.
after_edge: Write data tenure is also queued.

at_edge: CPU samples qualified DBG with DBWO asserted.
after_edge: CPU selects the queued write, asserts DBB, and drives write data ahead of the older read.

at_edge: Final write TA is accepted.
after_edge: CPU releases DBB; the older read remains queued.

at_edge: CPU samples a later qualified DBG with DBWO negated.
after_edge: CPU performs the outstanding read data tenure.

assertions: DBWO is sampled only with qualified DBG.
DBWO does not reorder writes relative to other writes.
If DBWO is asserted with no queued write, the next queued read proceeds.
Up to two data tenures can be queued; transactions from other masters may occur between these steps.

rules: CPU snoops address/attributes only in a TS cycle and uses GBL to qualify global coherence action.
Read or read-atomic hits can clean or flush; read-with-intent-to-modify hits flush; write-with-flush/write-with-kill actions invalidate and cancel reservation as Table 7-2 states.
A snoop hit on modified data requiring copyback asserts ARTRY, then the snooper requests address/data tenures for the push.
Figure 8-14 records Invalid, Exclusive, and Modified state transitions for WIM=001; CSE[0:1] identifies the selected set on CPU transactions.
unresolved: All Table 7-2 TT commands and all WIM cache modes need machine-readable transition rows.
Snoop push address/data beat ordering is not fully transcribed.

rules: Address and data buses arbitrate and transfer independently.
The processor has one additional level of address pipelining: as many as two address tenures can complete before the current data tenure completes.
Up to two data tenures can be queued.
Data normally follows address order; DBWO is the explicit write-before-older-read selection mechanism.
unresolved: Exact backpressure behavior when the second queued data tenure is occupied needs an implementation assertion tied to future bus RTL.

mode.selected_by: DRTRY asserted when HRESET is negated

rules: Read data is forwarded internally when TA is recognized without the normal following-cycle confirmation.
The system must never assert DRTRY after startup.

For generic/64-bit transactions ARTRY cancellation must occur before or coincident with the first TA, never in the following cycle. The explicit 32-bit exception uses the first TA for word or smaller and the second TA for double-word or burst transactions.
Other arbitration/transfer rules remain the same.
